item.title: API Reference
item.description: All API endpoints are served on the admin port (default :9090). Base path: /api/v1. Rules List Rules GET /api/v1/rules Returns all rules sorted by priority (ascending). Response: 200 OK [ { "id": "uuid", "enabled": true, "priority": 1, "action": "deny", "match": { "path_prefixes": ["/admin"] }, "description": "Block admin", "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" } ] Create Rule POST /api/v1/rules Request body: { "priority": 1, "action": "deny", "enabled": true, "description": "Block admin paths", "match": { "path_prefixes": ["/admin"] } } Response: 201 Created with the created rule (including generated id).

item.title: Architecture
item.description: System Components Network Guard Proxy consists of four main components: 1. Proxy Engine The proxy engine listens on the public port (default :8080) and handles all incoming HTTP requests. For each request it: Builds a request context (client IP, method, path, headers) Evaluates the filter chain against configured rules Either blocks the request (403 Forbidden) or forwards it to the upstream backend Logs the decision with latency information The engine is built on Go’s net/http/httputil.

item.title: Configuration Reference
item.description: Config File Network Guard Proxy reads its configuration from a YAML file specified via the --config flag: ./networkguard --config config.yaml Full Reference proxy: listen_address: ":8080" # Public proxy listener address upstream_url: "http://localhost:9000" # Backend to forward allowed requests admin: listen_address: ":9090" # Admin API and Web UI listener storage: driver: "sqlite" # Storage backend (currently only "sqlite") dsn: "./network_guard.db" # Database file path logging: level: "info" # Log level max_logs: 10000 # Maximum number of log entries to retain Configuration Fields Field Type Default Description proxy.

item.title: Getting Started
item.description: Prerequisites Go 1.24 or later Installation Clone the repository and build: git clone https://github.com/networkguard/proxy.git cd proxy go build ./cmd/networkguard/ Configuration Copy the example configuration: cp config.example.yaml config.yaml Edit config.yaml to set your upstream backend URL: proxy: listen_address: ":8080" upstream_url: "http://localhost:9000" admin: listen_address: ":9090" storage: driver: "sqlite" dsn: "./network_guard.db" logging: level: "info" max_logs: 10000 Running Start the proxy: ./networkguard --config config.yaml The proxy will listen on two ports: :8080 - Public proxy port (client traffic) :9090 - Admin port (API + Web UI) Quick Test You can set up a simple upstream server for testing:

item.title: Rule System
item.description: Overview Network Guard Proxy uses a priority-based rule system. Rules are evaluated in ascending priority order (lower number = higher priority). The first matching rule decides the action. If no rule matches, the default action is allow. Rule Structure Each rule has: priority (int): Evaluation order. Lower values are checked first. action (allow or deny): What to do when the rule matches. enabled (bool): Disabled rules are skipped during evaluation.

item.title: Web UI Guide
item.description: Accessing the Web UI The Web UI is served at the root of the admin port: http://localhost:9090/ No authentication is required (can be added behind a reverse proxy).
